findings.issue: `strip_comments` (l.96) and `declarations` (l.173, with NAMESPACE_RE/SECTION_RE/END_RE at l.82-85) re-implement `scripts/lean_source.py`'s `strip_comments_and_strings` (l.167) and `declarations`/`scopes`/`update_scope`/`qualified_declarations` (l.326/355/443/461), which already returns exactly the fully qualified per-file names this script's index needs. Two parsers for the same source language will drift: the local copy pops one scope per `end` regardless of name and only matches single-line `@[...]` attribute blocks, so its declaration index (which drives the published roadmap→module links and the dashed PhyslibAlpha-eligible marker) can disagree with the audit's.

findings.evidence: `roadmap_progress.py:141:def layer_id`, `:392:"layer_ids": [layer_id(t) for t in layers]`; grep of `roadmap/EpsilonEridaniRoadmaps/Diffraction/README.md:357` vs `Suggested.lean:99`.
findings.fix: Key the layer node on the shared id: import `layer_id` from `roadmap_progress` and use `roadmap:<Area>#<layer id>` (falling back to the section title when the heading has no layer lead), so a node id resolves to the same layer as `progress.json`'s `layer_ids`.
findings.issue: The roadmap layer inventory is a parallel API to the one the site already publishes: `roadmap_progress.py:115-143` derives layers and stable ids (`layer_id`) from each roadmap's README, while `read_roadmaps` here derives its own positional ids (`roadmap:<Area>/<stem>#<n>`) and titles from `Suggested.lean`. The two cannot be joined and disagree in wording — Diffraction README `## Layer 1: the diffractive cross section and the diffractive structure functions` vs Suggested.lean `## Layer 1: diffractive structure functions` — so Progress and Modules show different layer sets for the same roadmap.

summary: The generator re-implements the repository's shared Lean source parser (`scripts/lean_source.py`) and the site palette constants it already imports, and it builds a second, unjoinable roadmap-layer inventory beside the one `roadmap_progress.py` publishes. The graph/viewer itself is new work; the parsing and styling plumbing should come from the existing modules.
